transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, occupational health sent me here. They're saying I'm not eating enough to stay on duty. But honestly, most days I just have black coffee. Maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night if I have to. Having a full meal... it just feels like I'm letting my standards slip, you know?
Are you worried about gaining weight if you eat more than you currently do?

Yes, I am. Honestly, if I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this... this jolt, like I've completely lost control of things. If that happens, I just spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder. I just can't stand the idea of putting any weight back on.
Do you think you are currently at a healthy weight?

Well, I know what other people think. My uniform hangs off me now, and I've had to tighten my belt past all the old notches just to keep it on. But... honestly, when the nurse out front told me my weight was dangerously low, I didn't agree. My first thought was just, 'I could still stand to be a little sharper.' So, to me, it doesn't feel unhealthy, even if the numbers say otherwise.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?

No, I don't really do that. Like I said, I mostly just stick to my coffee or maybe a yogurt. The idea of eating a lot of food at once... that's just not something I do. I keep things pretty strictly controlled.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while you're eating?

No, not at all. It's... well, it's the exact opposite, really. I have complete control over everything I put in my body. I don't ever sit down and just... lose myself in a meal or feel like I can't stop. Like I said, I keep a very tight grip on what I eat, so losing control just isn't something that happens to me.
Have you ever had an episode of eating an excessive amount of food in a short period of time at any point in your life?

No, never. Even going back years... I just don't eat like that. I've never been the type to gorge myself or eat a huge amount of food in one sitting, at any point in my life. It's just never happened.
Is your decision to restrict your food intake driven by a fear of gaining weight?

Yes, it is. I mean... if I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this jolt, like I've completely lost control. When that happens, I'll spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder. I just can't stand the idea of putting any weight back on. So, yeah, that fear is exactly what drives it.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after eating to prevent weight gain?

No, I haven't done anything like that. I don't throw up or use laxatives or anything. I just... I manage it all by controlling what I eat in the first place. I don't need to do those other things because I don't let myself eat enough to need them.
Do you think your weight or body shape has anything to do with your self-worth?

Yeah, it does. Honestly, it has everything to do with it. When I look in the mirror... I just don't see what everyone else says they see. They might tell me one thing, but my eyes go right to my stomach and my waist. 

If I don't like what I see there... well, I basically judge my whole day by whether I look lean enough to actually respect myself. If I don't look tight and lean in those areas, I just don't feel like I'm worth much of anything. So, yeah, my self-worth is completely tied to it.
Have you ever felt like you were eating an amount of food that was larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time?

No, never. I... I keep a pretty tight grip on my eating. Like I said earlier, I restrict what goes in, so I've never had a time where I just lost control and ate a huge amount of food all at once. It's strictly the opposite for me.
